audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Theorem 4.8/D.5 fails for allowed Lipschitz activations; Theorem 4.9 fails for the stated arbitrary nonnegative loss; F.6 radius-only bound eliminates genuine sampling fluctuation.
limitations: 0047-P2 — Theorem 4.9 fails for the stated arbitrary nonnegative loss — Counterevidence: Shen v4 p.5 assumes [0,1]-valued hypotheses, absolute disagreement, shared labels and a common class Lipschitz constant. Its own result is not refuted. Separate transductive softmax does not restrict Eq. (6).

0047-P4 — The asserted exact-k nodal-domain existence is false — Counterevidence: Davies v1 distinguishes weak/strong domains and multiplicity-sensitive upper bounds; those are not universal exact-count existence assertions.

0047-P5 — Missing absolute value in signed-filter operator-norm bound — Counterevidence: The preceding operator-norm decomposition is valid and makes the intended response-magnitude reading inferable. However, the surrounding maximum-value prose repeats the unsigned quantity and directly uses it for the feature-stability claim. The absolute-value repair remains analytically verified; no empirical-score damage is inferred.
0047-P6 — Cheeger constant omits the operative cut-domain restriction — Counterevidence: Conventional volume/min-side definition restores this issue; no claim against standard Cheeger theorem.
Limits: No arbitrary merely Lipschitz nonpolynomial extension; remainder constant may depend on polynomial.

proposition.claim:
Output difference is controlled by coefficient-weighted or summed-depth modified tree distances under merely Lipschitz activations/readout.

Target risk <= source risk + 2 K_Lip W1 + best joint risk for the stated nonnegative-loss setup.

High-probability transductive gap bound proportional to radius R on the stated closed parameter ball.

At least one eigenvector at lambda_k has exactly k nodal domains.

Feature term bounded by sup h(lambda) instead of sup |h(lambda)|.

lambda2/2<=h<=sqrt(2lambda2) for printed h=min_S cut/(d|S|), with no half-size/volume restriction.
